passages.excerpt_preview: This technical history distinguishes Bose’s short-wave experimental program from the development of commercial wireless telegraphy.
Bose experimented at wavelengths from about 2.5 centimetres to 5 millimetres.
Some concepts from his 1897 work were later incorporated into a 1.3-millimetre multibeam receiver at the NRAO 12-m telescope.
axwell’s equations predicted electromagnetic radiation and Hertz demonstrated electromagnetic waves in 1888.
He used waveguides, horn antennas, dielectric lenses, polarizers and semiconductor detectors at frequencies as high as 60 GHz.
Bose described to the Royal Institution in 1897 research carried out in Calcutta at millimeter wavelengths.
His apparatus investigated reflection, refraction, polarization and other optical-like properties of short radio waves.
